solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Common weed of various colours, deep round inside

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, splitting the word for many-coloured in two

parts.note: pied means patched with several colours

indicators.note: turning something round sets it facing the other way, so the word for deep is read backwards

parts.note: a deep voice or note is a bass

explanation.surface: A botanist describes a familiar multicoloured weed with something deep and round at its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: PISSABED is an old dialect name for the dandelion, from its diuretic reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: The dandelion, a very common lawn weed, has long been called by this rustic name.

clue.text: Collage showing chemist finally serving prince in place of king

indicators.note: the change is made at the end of the chemist's name, on its final letter
the prince is serving, standing in to do another's job
one letter takes the position the other held, replacing it

parts.note: Louis Pasteur was the French chemist behind pasteurisation
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A chemist's shop where a prince stands in for the king at the end of the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' points at the last letter of PASTEUR, the R for king; 'serving ... in place of' puts the prince's P there instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A paste-up is a layout or collage made by pasting pieces of paper onto a backing sheet.

clue.text: Travel as young often do? I love going round the old world

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so the word for love wraps the next piece

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, nil
terra, Latin for earth or the world

explanation.surface: A traveller declares their love of touring the ancient world, as youngsters tend to.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a question because it defines by example: young backpackers famously use an Interrail pass to cross Europe by train.
explanation.definitionFit: To interrail is to tour Europe on a cheap rail pass, a classic gap-year pursuit of young people.

clue.text: Make engraving rarely an advantage put up round college

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up means writing it bottom to top
a word placed round another surrounds it

parts.note: a plus is an advantage
C is the abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: An engraver rarely gains any edge by raising things around a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rarely' belongs to the definition: SCULP is a rare verb meaning to carve or engrave.
explanation.definitionFit: Sculp is a seldom-used back-formation from sculpture, meaning to carve or engrave.

clue.text: Measure once adopted in Russia boyars hindered in part

indicators.note: only part of the words is used, so the answer sits within them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Russian nobles were partly held back by an old system of measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: Boyars were the old Russian aristocracy, which keeps the surface in Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: The arshin was an old Russian unit of length, roughly 71 centimetres.

clue.text: Cattle affliction: very young one is brought up with no change?

parts.note: a babe is a baby

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing a word up writes it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the word is, reversed
as is: unaltered

explanation.surface: A farm ailment strikes a newborn calf, which is reared without any alteration.
explanation.definitionFit: Babesiasis is a tick-borne parasitic disease of cattle, also known as redwater fever.

clue.text: Mugs spoke up about what's central to knowledge

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means written from bottom to top
about means placed around another piece

parts.note: said is the past tense of speak

indicators.note: the central letter of the following word is the one taken

parts.note: the fifth of nine letters

explanation.surface: Fools spoke out on the heart of learning.
explanation.walkthrough: Mugs suggests fools or cups; here it is slang for faces, as is dials.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mug and dial are British slang for a person's face.

clue.text: Fabulous tree, one inhabiting downs? Certainly not

indicators.note: something inhabiting a place lives inside it

parts.note: the opposite of downs
a means one

explanation.surface: A legendary tree, perhaps growing on the downs? Certainly not.
explanation.walkthrough: Downs suggests English chalk hills; it is just the opposite of ups.
explanation.definitionFit: The upas of Java was fabled to poison everything for miles around, hence a fabulous tree.

clue.text: Let loose, stop living having to accept rotten luck

indicators.note: having to accept means being made to take something in, so the word for stop living holds the jumbled letters inside

parts.note: unbe is an old word meaning to cease to exist

indicators.note: something rotten has decayed and fallen apart, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A doomed figure who, out of bad luck, must die and is finally set free.
explanation.walkthrough: UNBE is an archaic Chambers word for cease to be; 'rotten' rearranges LUCK into UCKL, which UNBE is 'having to accept' between UNB and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbuckle a strap is to unfasten it, setting it loose.

clue.text: Hide from downpour

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a heavy fall of rain

explanation.walkthrough: Hide reads as a verb, sheltering from the rain; it is the noun for an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelt is a fur skin, and as a noun pelt is also a heavy beating rainfall.

clue.text: Trooper in India well before hostilities

parts.note: so, as in 'well, then'
war is open hostilities

explanation.surface: An Indian soldier is fit and ready before fighting breaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: A sowar was a native cavalryman or mounted policeman in British India.

clue.text: Spanish lawman in core organized to protect urchin?

indicators.note: protecting shelters something, so the rearranged letters wrap around the urchin
organized means put into order, so these letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: a street arab is a dated term for a homeless urchin

explanation.surface: A core group arranged to look after a street child, by a Spanish policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organized' rearranges IN CORE into CINERO, and 'to protect' wraps it around ARAB after the C. 'Street arab' for an urchin is a dated, now offensive term.
explanation.definitionFit: A carabinero is a Spanish frontier guard or police officer, so a lawman of Spain.

clue.text: Horse painter setting aside barrel inside for farrier's scraps

indicators.note: setting something aside removes it, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: George Stubbs, the great painter of horses
B is an abbreviation for barrel; one of the inner Bs goes

explanation.surface: An equine artist lays aside a cask to keep a blacksmith's offcuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubs are the worn ends of old horseshoe nails, leftovers from a farrier's work.

clue.text: Ogre once presented in Fleet Street displaying charming quality

indicators.note: something presented in a place appears inside it

parts.note: Fleet Street is shorthand for the British newspaper industry
ettin is an archaic word for a giant

explanation.surface: An old monster appears in the London newspaper world and proves surprisingly charming.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street in London was home to the national newspapers, so it stands for the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Prettiness is the attractive, pleasing quality of something charming to look at.

clue.text: Like a puffer, line entering a bend?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something entering a space goes inside it

parts.note: to bow is to bend
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A puffer fish, perhaps, swims a line into a curve.
explanation.walkthrough: Puffer suggests the fish; here it is anything that blows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablow is an old adverb meaning in a state of blowing, as a puffer is.

clue.text: Form of help cutting monstrosity as abandoned, cable system

indicators.note: cutting into something places a piece within it
abandoned letters are left out of the word

parts.note: teras is a term for a monstrosity or malformed creature
taken as written, then removed

indicators.note: a new form of a word reshapes its letters

parts.note: rearranged

explanation.surface: Some kind of help cuts down a monster that has been left behind, via cable.
explanation.definitionFit: A telpher is an overhead cable or rail line along which loads are carried electrically.

clue.text: Delicate material indeed disheartened young in lesson (9, two words)

parts.note: la is an old interjection meaning indeed

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a class is a lesson

indicators.note: losing its heart leaves only a word's outermost letters

parts.note: the first and last letters only

explanation.surface: Fine stuff indeed for a downhearted youngster in class.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacy glass is pressed glassware with a fine stippled pattern, delicate like lace.

clue.text: Night-time attack happened, catching one stiff

indicators.note: catching means the happened word holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: came, as in 'came about', means happened
one is the Roman numeral I
sad describes bread or pastry that is heavy and stiff

explanation.surface: A raid by night took place and caught a corpse.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers gives sad as heavy or stiff, of bread or pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisade is an old military term for a surprise attack made at night.

clue.text: Search in litter for portion of dead tissue

indicators.note: litter is mess and disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone rummages through rubbish for a scrap of dead flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: An eschar is a dry scab or slough of dead skin, as after a burn.

clue.text: Townie to join, taking in renovated bar

indicators.note: the word for join takes the rearranged letters into its middle

parts.note: to unite is to join together

indicators.note: a renovated place is remodelled, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A town dweller signing up to a group that has taken over a refurbished pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' and 'renovated' suggest a pub refit, but the bar is just three letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An urbanite is a city or town dweller, which a townie is in informal speech.

clue.text: Throwing away half, keep odd bits of cake, making one feel sick

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is two letters, and the second pair is thrown away
the odd bits are the letters in odd positions, the first and third

parts.note: the first and third letters of cake are C and K

explanation.surface: Someone who, after binning half their dessert, keeps the odd bits and ends up queasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throwing away half' drops EP from KEEP to leave KE; 'odd bits of cake' gives CK.
explanation.definitionFit: Keck is a dialect verb meaning to retch or heave, as when nauseated.

clue.text: The first always comes last after spirit has left

indicators.note: after places the phrase before it behind the pieces that follow it

parts.note: ka is the spirit or soul in Egyptian belief
L for left
something that comes last ends things

explanation.surface: Whatever is first always ends up last once the soul departs.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opening words: the kalends are, always, the first day of the Roman month.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar the kalends (calends) were the first day of every month.

clue.text: Winner's achievement among principal models

indicators.note: among says the answer is found within the letters of the next words

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A prizewinner's success stands out among the leading catwalk models.
explanation.definitionFit: The palm is a symbol of victory, so to bear or carry off the palm is to win.

clue.text: Herd always rejected orchid

parts.note: cattle are animals kept in a herd

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: ay is an old word for always or ever

explanation.surface: A herd of cows that always turns its nose up at the flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns AY, a variant of aye meaning ever, into YA.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattleya is a genus of showy tropical American orchids, named after William Cattley.

clue.text: Mount rode up, showing overlapping piece of armour

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tel is an ancient mound or hill
sat, as on a horse

explanation.surface: A rider mounted and rode uphill in jointed armour.
explanation.walkthrough: Mount seems a verb or a horse; it is a hill, the tel of Middle Eastern archaeology.
explanation.definitionFit: A taslet (tasset) is one of the overlapping plates guarding the thigh in a suit of armour.

clue.text: Teacher is welcoming university star outshining the rest

parts.note: pupils call a male teacher sir

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them in, so a piece goes inside

parts.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster welcomes the university's brightest student.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirius, the Dog Star, is the brightest star in the night sky.

clue.text: Cooked pastry base shouldn't be like this, very like an omelette (first off)!

definitions.text: Cooked pastry base shouldn't be like this

indicators.note: taking the first off drops the opening letter

parts.note: so means very
full of egg

explanation.surface: A baker warns that pastry should never turn out damp and eggy.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'soggy bottom', undercooked pastry, is a famous fault on British baking shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Soggy means wet and limp, the classic failing of an underbaked pastry case.

clue.text: Like votes when cast under being distributed

indicators.note: distributed things are spread about, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: rearranged

explanation.surface: Ballots once cast are handed out under supervision.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast votes are placed in a ballot urn, so they are urned, put in an urn.

clue.text: Revolution contained by papacy, clearly

indicators.note: the answer is held within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters span the two words

explanation.surface: An uprising is plainly being held in check by the Pope.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolution suggests a political uprising; here it is a single turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A cycle is one complete turn or rotation, as a revolution is.

clue.text: Performance by Serbs, look, dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters move around into new positions

parts.note: rearranged

explanation.surface: Watch a Serbian group perform their dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The kolo is a Serbian circle dance performed by a ring of dancers.

clue.text: The old rise in line dressed grandly (7, two words)

indicators.note: the old word goes in among the rearranged letters
dressing a shop window arranges its contents, so these letters are arranged anew

parts.note: sty is an obsolete word meaning to rise or climb

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned rise of a line of people, all dressed up grandly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed' seems to belong with 'grandly' in the definition, but it is the anagram signal for 'line'. STY, to rise, is a Spenserian word found in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in style means doing it with elegance and splendour, so grandly.

clue.text: Deep sound ordinary in piccolo? The opposite

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: piccolo is Italian for small; gran(de) is Italian for big
O is the abbreviation for ordinary

explanation.surface: A low note from something ordinary inside a piccolo, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The piccolo looks like the instrument, but it is read as the Italian word for small.
explanation.definitionFit: A groan is a deep, low sound of pain or dismay.

clue.text: Classical poet, one that disappeared mysteriously

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Roman poet of the Pharsalia
second meaning: the British earl who vanished in 1974

explanation.walkthrough: Lord Lucan, a British peer, vanished in 1974 after his children's nanny was murdered and was never found.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a Roman epic poet and a notorious vanished aristocrat bear this name.

clue.text: Medicinal root of yesteryear taken in as gel, mixed (10, two words)

indicators.note: the old-time word is taken into the middle of the mixed letters
mixed means stirred together, so these letters are combined in a new order

parts.note: olden means belonging to former times, of yesteryear

explanation.surface: An old herbal remedy swallowed down in gel form after mixing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges AS GEL into GSEAL, which has OLDEN 'taken in' after its G.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldenseal is a North American plant whose yellow root is used in herbal medicine.

clue.text: Poet's since disheartened young with Old English

indicators.note: losing its heart leaves only a word's outermost letters

parts.note: first and last letters only
OE is the abbreviation for Old English

explanation.surface: A poet has been gloomy ever since youth, writing in Old English.
explanation.definitionFit: Ygoe is a Spenserian word meaning ago, or since, used only in poetry.

clue.text: Difficulty is time getting into clothes

indicators.note: getting into something puts it inside

parts.note: dress means clothing
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: The trouble is that dressing takes ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is a state of hardship or difficulty, as in a ship in distress.
